## Open

### F-001 — Rewriting a whole file is only safe when fences are tracked

> _2026-09-15 · tools/blong-dev · open_

The first version of the blank-line handling collapsed runs inside fenced code blocks, which
silently changes a sample that contains a blank line. The wrapper now tracks fences, and leaves
tables, headings, the meta line and HTML comments alone. Lesson: a formatter that rewrites a file
has to model the syntax it must preserve, not only the syntax it changes.

### F-002 — A move between two root areas deleted the entry

> _2026-09-15 · tools/blong-dev · open_

move read the target file, inserted the entry, then removed it from the source read taken earlier.
When both areas live in the same file (cross-cutting to ci) those were the same document: the entry
was written twice and then removed once, so it vanished. Found by smoke testing the verbs in a
scratch workspace rather than by the unit tests, which each covered one operation in isolation. The
fix edits the meta line in place when the target is the same file.

### F-003 — A second write to the same file overwrote the first batch

> _2026-09-15 · tools/blong-dev · open_

migrate grouped work by area, but every root area (cross-cutting, ci, docs) lives in the same root
document: the second area rebuilt the document from the skeleton and wrote it over the first batch,
silently dropping 18 entries. Group by target file, keep one document per file, write once.

### F-004 — A stale line range spliced items into the index block

> _2026-09-15 · tools/blong-dev · open_

ensureManualSection returned the section parsed before refreshIndex moved the file, so
addManualItems spliced the 32 migrated manual items inside the index block; the next refresh
replaced that range and the items were gone, with no error. Re-read the structure after the refresh:
any line range from parseDoc is invalidated by a refresh.

### F-130 — `tap`'s positional globs bypass its own `exclude` rules

> _2026-09-12 · tools/blong-dev · open_

`blong-dev test` passes `'*.test.ts' '**/*.test.ts'` as positional test files, and tap then ignores
both its default excludes (folders named `dist`, `fixture`, `fixtures`) and an explicit
`--exclude=…`, so a package's generated fixture directory runs as part of the package suite.

Four things were tried before accepting that: `--exclude` after the globs, `--exclude` before them,
a negated glob (`'!test/fixture/**'`), and dropping the globs entirely. Dropping them works, but
tap's default `include` then also picks up Playwright specs and layer files that merely live under
`test/`.

Fixing it properly means `blong-dev test` honoring a package-level tap config instead of hard-coding
globs — a shared-tool change with repo-wide blast radius.

### F-081 — The blong-dev package has no ci-test script and no eslint config

> _2026-09-12 · tools/blong-dev · open_

`tools/blong-dev` has no `ci-test` script, so `npm run ci-test` there errors, and it has no eslint
config either, so `blong-dev lint` prints two check marks instead of three. Both are normal for this
package: neither is a failure, and neither should be "fixed" as part of an unrelated change.

### F-201 — A comma in a memory title is silently rejected

> _2026-09-19 · tools/blong-dev · open_

blong-dev memory add decision --title with a comma in it prints the command usage instead of an
error naming the bad value, so the entry is simply not written and nothing says why. Cost two
attempts here; the body may contain commas, the title may not. A title with a comma should either be
taken literally or refused with a message that names it.

### F-217 — memory add rejects a colon in the title, and says nothing useful about it

> _2026-09-21 · tools/blong-dev · open_

A title containing a colon - "A condition that had always been an object: fixing it..." - makes
`blong-dev memory add` print the whole memory usage block instead of an error, so the entry is
simply not written and the reason is not stated. It cost two attempts to spot, because the same body
text with a colon-free title is accepted and the `add` verb takes no `--body-file`, so the first fix
attempt was invalid for a second reason. Worth either quoting the offending argument or rejecting it
by name.

## Resolved

### F-080 — `blong-dev` CLI not built

> _2026-09-11 · tools/blong-dev · resolved_

— `npm run ci-lint` (`blong-dev lint`) fails with
`Cannot find module .../blong-dev/bin/blong-dev.ts`, so eslint/cspell could not be run from the
package. Fell back to the VS Code `get_errors` diagnostics (clean) + file-local cspell disables.
Needs a `rush build` of `tools/blong-dev` to run the real lint locally.

### F-090 — `blong-dev` was not built, so `npm run ci-lint` could not find it

> _2026-09-12 · tools/blong-dev · resolved_

`npm run ci-lint` (`blong-dev lint`) failed with
`Cannot find module .../blong-dev/bin/blong-dev.ts`, so eslint and cspell could not be run from the
package. The fallback was the VS Code `get_errors` diagnostics (clean) plus file-local
`/* spell-checker: disable */` comments, which is the repo's documented convention for theme files.

Running the real lint locally needs a `rush build` of `tools/blong-dev` first.

### F-103 — `blong-dev sql` went unused because the dev DB name was unknown

> _2026-08-19 · tools/blong-dev · resolved_

`blong-dev sql` now derives the dev DB name (`${suite}-${user}`, e.g. `blong-access-kalin`) when
none is configured — from the `.blong_devrc` `suite` key, else the `package.json` name in the cwd,
else `--suite`; the user comes from the OS user — and renders `${suite}`/`${user}` templates. It is
documented as the intended way to query the DB in the blong-schema and blong-adapter skills and in
`copilot-instructions.md`, to be used instead of a MySQL CLI or `kubectl exec`.

### F-104 — `blong-dev sql` connected as an anonymous user

> _2026-08-21 · tools/blong-dev · resolved_

`readConnection` started from `{}` and only layered `.blong_devrc`/CLI values, so with no `srv.db`
in `.blong_devrc` the connection had no user or password and MySQL answered
`Access denied for user ''@'...'`. The fix falls back to the shared `srv.db` adapter's dev defaults
(`blong-admin`/`password` at `localhost:3306`) for the default `srv.db` key only — custom `--config`
keys stay empty — and auto-creates the derived dev database (`${suite}-${user}`) when it is missing,
mirroring the dev intent's `createDatabase: true`. A dev tool should mirror the framework's own dev
connection defaults instead of requiring per-developer `.blong_devrc` setup.
